findings.title: The state flip-flop specification does not enforce validity of st_d, so an illegal st_d can propagate to st_q, causing the FSM to leave the defined state space and potentially corrupt HMAC operation.
findings.contradiction: The assumption incorrectly claims no recovery for st_d X, while the combinational next-state logic provides a default case that recovers to StIdle. This is a specification/documentation inconsistency.

evidence.excerpt: st_q is always one of the defined states (StIdle, StIPad, StMsg, StWaitResp, StPushToMsgFifo, StOPad, StDone). risk: If st_q is corrupted to an invalid value, the default case forces st_d=StIdle, but
st_q is asynchronously forced to StIdle when rst_ni is low; otherwise st_q updates to st_d on every positive edge of clk_i.
No recovery mechanism exists if st_d becomes X; st_q would capture X and the FSM could enter an illegal state.
In any unspecified state (default case), st_d=StIdle, leaving all other outputs at their default values (G1).
